notes:
Account snapshot and negotiation notes:
- Primary contact: CTO Priya Desai (concern: trading signal availability during US market hours).
- Business driver: house real-time trading signals and risk scoring; downtime impacts P&L directly.
- Delivery model desired: Redwood Dedicated in VPC with optional on-prem burst for regulatory audits.
- SLA asks from Argentum: 99.95% uptime minimum, 99.99% for trading-critical endpoints if possible; credits for downtime on per-hour and per-month basis.
- Support expectations: P1 response <= 30 minutes for production outages (phone + Slack), P2 <= 4 hours, 24x7 escalation.
- Maintenance windows: prefer scheduled maintenance outside US market hours (00:00-04:00 ET) and at most 2 planned windows / quarter; Argentum wants a 14-day notice for non-emergency maintenance.
- Credit schedule proposed by Argentum: sliding scale starting at 5% service credit for monthly uptime < 99.95%, 10% for <99.9%, escalates to contract termination trigger at sustained <99.5% over 3 months. Redwood draft proposes different bands; legal to reconcile.
- Throughput / reserved GPU planning: target reserved capacity = equivalent of 8x A100-80GB (or 4x H100) with sustained throughput target ~5k tokens/sec across concurrent model pool; need headroom for 2x burst.
- Latency SLOs: p50 target ~40-60ms, p95 target <=120ms for 1k-token chat. Argentum insists p99 be included in monitoring (informational).
- Fallbacks: must have automated fallback to smaller model variant within same capacity tier for overload periods; Redwood to document routing policies and fallbacks.
- Data residency: logs and KV cache must remain in US-only region; audit logs retained for 7 years (finance requirement).
- Quote/Commercial: preliminary Dedicated price attached (drive link). Client asks for 12-month committed reservation + 1-month pilot.
- Risk notes: procurement flags credit schedule as primary blocker; finance needs clearer penalty vs termination thresholds.
- Quote from CTO on call: "We can accept 99.95% for non-trading endpoints but trading feed must be locked to higher SLA or dedicated failover."
- Next actions: legal to exchange redlines on SLA; Redwood infra to run final benchmark (p95 + throughput) on dedicated config; SE/CSM to prepare runbook for on-call and incident paths.
